name: Missing or wrong access control on privileged function
requires: the contract source or verified bytecode, including inherited bases
at least one externally reachable function that writes privileged state or moves value
a way to execute it as an unprivileged account (fork test or local deployment)
questions: Is there any modifier or in-body check on this exact function, and does it compare the caller against the correct subject?
Is the check inherited, and does the inherited implementation read a slot an attacker cannot write?
Under a meta-transaction forwarder (ERC2771), does every authorization path use _msgSender() rather than raw msg.sender?
Once an attacker calls it, what is the maximum damage: full drain, bounded fee change, one-time flag, or nothing observable?
Does the function let the caller choose the beneficiary (mint to, withdraw to, upgrade to) as well as trigger the action?
Which account can actually reach the implementation's initialize or reinitialize, and is that restriction a real modifier rather than a self-service call any role can make?
Is tx.origin used for authorization anywhere in the call path?
Is the role-granting function guarded by the admin role specifically, or can a low-privilege role escalate itself?
false_positives: A guard exists under a project-specific name (auth, restricted, onlyGovernance) that was not read
The function is internal or private and its single caller carries the gate
The role holder is a timelocked governance contract, making the issue centralisation rather than broken access control
An unguarded setter bounded to a harmless range, such as a fee that can only move by one basis point
Test, mock, or script contracts that are never deployed
onlyOwner on a function whose only effect is on the owner's own funds
An open renounceOwnership that bricks admin functions without touching user funds
A constructor mistaken for a callable initializer, when no initializer actually exists
poc_must_show: a freshly generated EOA with no roles calling the function successfully
the privileged effect read back from state (owner, implementation slot, fee, minted balance, paused flag)
a control call by a legitimately privileged account producing the same effect
for a drain, the attacker balance delta and the protocol loss in token units
for a proxy initializer, the implementation address called and the storage slot written
impact_bar: Reportable when an unprivileged account can move or destroy funds, replace the implementation, mint supply, change a trusted price, or lock users out of their own funds, with the amount or slot named. Informational for missing guards with bounded harmless effect or centralisation observations about a legitimate admin.
